[SWS_CM_00143] Minimum Send Interval monitoring for transmission requests for Fields
⌈
To protect receivers from flooding/overload, each field shall have a config-
urable Minimum Send Interval (see ServiceInterfaceDeploymentElement.min-
imumSendInterval), which specifies the minimum amount of time that shall pass be-
tween two consecutive transmissions, i.e., the Minimum Send Interval limits the max-
imum Tx frequency of a given field in the network. If the application requests trans-
mission of a field by calling Field::Update()/Update(), ara::com shall check, whether the time since the last successful handover of the field to the underlying trans-
mission layer is greater than the specified Minimum Send Interval, i.e., the Minimum
Send Interval is not violated. If the field has never been sent before, this shall also suc-
cessfully pass the Minimum Send Interval check. If the Minimum Send Interval is not
violated, ara::com shall process the transmission request by handing over the field
to the transmission layer. The time of handover shall count as start of the new Min-
imum Send Interval monitoring. If the Minimum Send Interval is violated, ara::com
shall discard the transmission request and return error kMinimumSendIntervalVi-
olationError (see [SWS_CM_10432]). If the configured Minimum Send Interval (
ServiceInterfaceDeploymentElement.minimumSendInterval) of a field has
the value 0, the Minimum Send Interval monitoring shall not be active for the corre-
sponding field.
